mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above trend while the signal persists.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or unemployment falls sharply while the signal is active.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds above trend before the horizon ends.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or inflation falls below 2% before the horizon ends.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household formation and spending, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered months, or housing starts fall while income continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above trend for three consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer demand and corporate profitability, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or payroll employment falls sharply before the horizon ends.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 4% YoY for two consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which increases earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO YoY growth > 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or industrial production decelerates before the horizon ends.
